title: The categorical palette fails colour-blind separation, and small marks need a ramp that does not
foundBy: consumer report (host): an application consuming this package, moving from 0.2.0 to 0.3.0, with measurements and reproduction steps

evidence.verified:
`node scripts/check-palette.mjs` holds each palette to the contract section 4.12 states for it, and all four hold. `--color-cat-*` has a separation of 9.4 dark and 8.0 light across six adjacent pairs. `--color-graph-*` separates by 9.6 dark and 10.0 light across all 28 pairs of its eight slots, against a floor of 8.

The values were confirmed against an independent implementation of the same published maths. It reports the same figures and passes all five of its checks in both themes, including the normal-vision floor at 16.6 dark and 15.6 light. `scripts/check-palette.test.mjs` passes 5 tests holding this implementation to figures that implementation produced, including a separation of 1.0 between two categorical slots under protanopia.

Measured in the published build rather than the source: `dist/lib/chartTheme.js` reads the new tokens, `dist/lib/chartTheme.d.ts` declares `graph` and `graphOther`, and `dist/styles/tokens.css` carries all 18 declarations. `npm run ci` exits 0 at 49a4437 with the palette check running inside `npm run check`, which is what the workflow runs. The visual gate compared 112 of 112 captures at 0 differing pixels.

details:
A consumer draws node-link diagrams over a model of 353 nodes and 411 edges, at dots of 3 to 5 pixels and lines of 1 pixel. They report that `--color-cat-1..10` does not hold at that mark size, and ask for a second ramp rather than hand-rolling one downstream.

Measured with the palette validator from the `dataviz` skill, which runs five checks: lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair separation under colour-blind simulation, normal-vision separation, and contrast against the surface.

Nine of the ten base slots fail four of the five checks on the dark surface. Separation under deuteranopia falls to 1.8 between `#6ab0d4` and `#c489c9`, and normal-vision separation falls to 12.2 between `#4fb3a6` and `#6f93c9`, under a floor of 15. The light set fails the same way.

The `-mid` sub-shades are the obvious alternative and they also fail. Separation under deuteranopia is 1.8 between `#0ea5e9` and `#d946ef` on the dark set, and 2.5 between `#0369a1` and `#a21caf` on the light set.

The consumer has nine categories, and reports that every nine-hue set they tested merges a pair under deuteranopia or protanopia. They therefore ask for eight slots and a defined neutral, which matches the documented rule that a ninth category folds to "Other" rather than becoming a generated hue.

The proposal is `--color-graph-1..8` for small marks, leaving `--color-cat-*` untouched for bar charts, with `--color-graph-other` aliased to `--color-structural`. The light values are `#2a78d6`, `#e26432`, `#189d6e`, `#bb7f00`, `#cc6c90`, `#008300`, `#4a3aa7` and `#e34948`. The dark values are `#3987e5`, `#d95926`, `#199e70`, `#c98500`, `#d55181`, `#008300`, `#9085e9` and `#e66767`.

Those values pass all five checks in both themes. Worst colour-blind separation is 8.7 light and 8.4 dark, worst normal-vision separation is 16.6 light and 19.3 dark, and every slot clears 3:1 contrast. The light surface tested was `#ffffff` and the dark surface `#0f1620`.

Upgrading does not escape the problem. `src/styles/tokens.css` is byte-identical between the `v0.3.0` tag and main at 8ada6d1, and no `--color-graph-*` token exists.

notes.text: Every figure the reporter gave was re-run against the same validator before filing, and all five palettes reproduce exactly, including the two weaknesses they disclosed themselves. The first is a tritan separation of 3.7 between the proposed light slots 3 and 4. The second is a colour-blind margin of 8.4 to 8.7 that clears the floor of 8 with little room. That margin means the ramp needs documenting as requiring secondary encoding, such as a legend, a label or a hover, rather than as safe on colour alone.

The report frames `--color-cat-*` as a good bar-chart palette that is poor for small marks. The measurements do not support the first half. A deuteranopia separation of 1.8 means two slots are the same colour, and a larger mark does not separate them. So adding a second ramp leaves the existing one failing for everyone who uses it, which makes this a wider decision than an additive token.

Against that, the validator is a tool from an external skill rather than a gate this repository adopted, and there is no palette gate here. `src/styles/tokens.css` records a review of the palette on 2026-08-27 against a real 1,366-event strip in both themes. Whether these thresholds become the standard is a decision rather than a correction.

The report cited a seven-character sha for main to support its claim that the palette is unchanged. That commit was a ledger commit on an unmerged branch, made the day the report was written, and it touched no stylesheet. This record cites the tag comparison instead. Recorded because a wrong sha that still resolves against this repository passes the freshness gate while meaning something else.

The reporter withdrew the framing that this is a small-mark problem, and named the mechanism instead. What separates the two regimes is which pairs of hues can ever touch. A bar, line or stacked chart only asks whether one series is distinct from its neighbour. A node-link diagram asks it of every pair, because any category can land beside any other.

Measured on the base palette against `#0f1620`, comparing adjacent pairs with all pairs. At five slots, adjacent separation passes at 9.4 while all-pairs separation falls to 0.9 between `#9e90cc` and `#6f93c9` under protanopia. At seven slots, adjacent warns at 6.4 and all-pairs stays at 0.9. At nine slots, adjacent fails at 1.8 and all-pairs falls to 0.5 between `#c489c9` and `#9e90cc`. Every figure was reproduced before this note was written.

Worse, the palette is below the normal-vision floor at two slots. `--color-cat-1` and `--color-cat-2` separate by 12.2 against a floor of 15, and both sit below the chroma floor. That is the first two series of any chart drawn with this palette.

This explains why the worked examples never surfaced it. `patterns/Chart.md` demonstrates a bar chart, a sankey diagram and a line chart, which are all adjacent-pair forms at series counts where the adjacent column still passes or warns. The gap was invisible by construction rather than by oversight. The legend example in that same document paints with `theme.categorical[0]` and `theme.categorical[1]`, which is the pair that misses the normal-vision floor.

There are two consequences for the decision. A ramp's contract states more usefully as a pair regime than as a mark size, because a consumer can tell whether any pair of their series may touch. And the scope is wider than an additive token, since the default palette misses a floor in the common case rather than only in a specialised one.

One distinction to carry into the spec decision, because it splits the question in two. The floors themselves, 15 for normal vision and 8 for colour-blind separation, are the validator's policy and are arguable. A protan separation of 0.9, or 0.5, is not a threshold question. At that distance two hues are the same colour for those readers under any standard.

So rejecting the thresholds does not dispose of the palette question. It changes which parts survive. The all-pairs collapse survives on its own terms, and the two-slot normal-vision miss depends on accepting a floor of 15.

The scope was decided by the owner. Each palette carries a stated contract and is held to that contract rather than to the other's.

`--color-cat-*` is safe where only adjacent series meet, which is a bar, line or stacked chart. It is fixed only as far as that contract requires. `--color-graph-*` is safe where any pair may meet, which is a node-link diagram, a scatter or a small multiple. It carries eight slots and a neutral.

The separation floors are adopted as this project's standard, and a check enforces them so neither palette drifts. A contract without a gate becomes a comment nobody re-runs. This repository keeps finding that a check which cannot run where the work happens reports its failure to whoever merges.

Two consequences to settle while writing the contracts. The adjacent contract cannot claim ten slots, because the palette passes adjacent separation at five, warns at seven and fails at nine. Either the failing slots move or the documented count is capped. And the pair of slots that misses the normal-vision floor sits inside the adjacent contract at any count, so it needs a decision either way.

Two rules for the contract, supplied by the reporter from five real drawings rather than from principle.

An empty category is absent rather than neutral. Four of their five drawings populate fewer than eight categories, and an unpopulated one draws no mark and no legend row. The neutral is only ever for the overflow past eight. Without saying so, an implementer reaches for the neutral to mean empty and the two meanings collide.

Slots are assigned from a fixed declared order, never by size or rank. The smallest populated category is different in every one of their drawings. A rule that folds the smallest would move the neutral between drawings and change a category's colour depending on which drawing is open. Colour follows the entity rather than its rank, and the neutral always takes the same ninth position.

Their taxonomy declares nine categories. All nine appear together in one drawing of the five, where the ninth carries two elements out of 442. So eight slots and a neutral cost that consumer two marks on one drawing and nothing on the other four.

First two steps landed in ce9f818. Section 4.12 of the design system specification now states a contract for each palette, and `--color-graph-1..8` and `--color-graph-other` exist in both themes. Nothing consumes them yet, so the visual gate compared 112 of 112 captures at 0 differing pixels.

The eight values were validated again after they were in `src/styles/tokens.css`, read back out of the file rather than taken from the report. Both themes pass all five checks, with worst colour-blind separation of 8.4 dark and 8.7 light.

The count the categorical palette can claim was measured rather than assumed, and it is six. Adjacent separation holds at 9.4 dark and 8.0 light through six slots. At seven it falls to 6.4 dark and 4.4 light, and the light theme is the binding constraint.

That matters for what remains. A separation of 4.4 sits under the floor of 6, so seven slots cannot be rescued by secondary encoding either. The specification now says the palette holds to six, and that slots seven to ten are not guaranteed separable.

The earlier report measured the dark theme and the light theme was not checked. Light is worse at every count past five.

The proposed ramp did not meet the regime it was proposed for, and the gate found it on its first run. The report validated those values with the tool's default, which compares adjacent pairs only. Their whole purpose is the case where any pair can meet.

Measured on all pairs, the proposal separated by 1.6 dark and 1.9 light under deuteranopia. Worse, it missed the normal-vision floor as well, at 7.1 dark and 6.1 light against a floor of 15. Its orange and its red were hard to tell apart for a reader with full colour vision. Seven of 28 pairs fell under that floor in the dark theme and six of 28 in the light one.

The same error was repeated in this session before it was caught. The adjacent figures were re-run, agreed with, and written into the specification as though they answered the all-pairs question.

Replacement values were searched against the checks rather than chosen, and they hold. On all pairs they separate by 9.6 dark and 10.0 light under colour blindness, against a target of 8. For normal vision they separate by 16.6 and 15.6, against a floor of 15. Every one of the five checks passes in both themes, confirmed against an independent implementation.

Lightness is what made it possible. A colour-blind reader keeps lightness when hue collapses, so spreading lightness across the slots separates eight of them where hue alone separates three. The cost is that the ramp looks less composed than the muted categorical set, which was the trade the owner accepted.

An earlier attempt searched each theme on its own and passed every check, then had to be thrown away. Its slots drifted up to 59 degrees of hue between the themes, so a category would have changed colour when the reader toggled. The categorical palette holds that drift to 8 degrees. The values that shipped fix the hue angles from the dark theme and solve only lightness and chroma for the light one, which keeps the drift inside 8.

Eight is what colour carries here, and the specification now says what to do at nine rather than leaving it to the reader. Fold the remainder into the neutral, add a channel colour does not use, or use small multiples.

A second neutral is the wrong answer and the specification says so. Low chroma reads as structural, and this project already spends that on the overflow slot and on de-emphasis. Naming selection as a second channel came from the owner. A reader who can isolate one category resolves a collision that a legend cannot, because a legend does not tell two adjacent dots apart.

The gate went in before the values were replaced, which is why the false claim was caught rather than shipped. Had the remediation come first, the specification would have carried a number nobody re-measured, and the check would have been written to agree with it.

`npm run check` was the right home for it. The workflow runs that and one job per linter, so a check added to the local mirror alone would have run on a contributor's machine and nowhere else.
